audit.whatIsWrong: The two sides disagree and I could not resolve it from data. This page reads Skill / Yone / Yone / Skill / Skill / Yone / Yone; the packet levelChart reads Yone on all seven rows at 52.04% over 1693 games; the already-audited mirror settled on Skill / Gragas / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Skill / Yone.
audit.why: Flipping Levels 2, 4-5 and 6 to Gragas to match the mirror would contradict both this packet and every whys[] row on this page, and I have no kit evidence for a Gragas power window — Barrel Roll is a telegraphed lob, Body Slam is 14s at rank 1, and neither beats your 4s Mortal Steel chain. Inventing that shift is exactly what the brief forbids, so I left the chart untouched and flagged it.
audit.corrected: No chart edit proposed — see questionsForUser. Everything else on the page was audited normally.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldowns anywhere in the spike or trade text.
audit.why: Barrel Roll is 10s at rank 1 falling to 6s; Body Slam 14s to 12s; Drunken Rage a 5s auto-reset that also reduces damage taken; Explosive Cask 100/85/70s. Your Soul Unbound runs 22s to 10s and Fate Sealed 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Trade inside the 14-second Body Slam window; treat Drunken Rage's one-second sample as the burst tell rather than the cast you react to.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fate Sealed described as setting up 'team knockups nothing can dodge'; Explosive Cask implied to be a knockup; Drunken Rage treated as something you simply all-in through.
audit.why: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward Yone — no airborne, and the kit carries no knockup flag. Explosive Cask knocks BACK, which is why it can throw you toward his team rather than off him. Drunken Rage reduces the damage Gragas receives and empowers his next basic attack as an auto-reset, so his combo opens with the wind-up, not with a cast you can see land. Body Slam is the stun that Barrel Roll's slow sets up, so dodging the cask denies the engage.
audit.corrected: Dodge Barrel Roll and Body Slam usually never lands. Drunken Rage cuts the damage he takes for a beat — open with Mortal Steel's airborne and cash out after it lapses. Fate Sealed pulls; Explosive Cask knocks back.

audit.why: Happy Hour heals on every skill use, so the existing early Executioner's Calling line is justified here.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last enemy and pulls; it never knocks up. Explosive Cask is 100s at rank 1 and knocks back, not up.

edits.before: Fate Sealed sets up team knockups nothing can dodge — build your teamfight around that. Gragas carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Fate Sealed pulls the enemies it clips toward you rather than knocking them up. Gragas carry threat: 7/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.after: Body Slam is his engage: 14s at rank 1, 12s at 5. Trade inside it.

edits.before: Track Gragas's Body Slam: His engage. Dodge it. When it is down — Q3-R him.
edits.after: Body Slam: 14s at rank 1, 12s at 5. Drunken Rage cuts damage he takes.

edits.before: That is Gragas's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Body Slam stuns, and Barrel Roll's slow is what lets him land it — dodge the cask.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Barrel Roll hits harder the longer it sits — leave before it detonates.

edits.before: Your first-item spike outpaces his — you all-in through Drunken Rage (W) with Q3 knockup + R while his cooldowns are long and his damage stays flat.
edits.after: Your first-item spike outpaces his — Drunken Rage cuts the damage he takes for a beat, so open with Q3's knockup and cash out once it lapses.

notes: The level chart is a genuine three-way conflict: this packet says Yone on all seven rows, the mirror's audit settled on Gragas winning Levels 2, 4-5 and 6, and this page currently sits between the two. I did not propose chart edits — flipping toward the mirror means asserting Gragas power windows that neither this packet nor his kit supports, and the brief forbids inventing a power shift. tools/mirror-fix.js will arbitrate; the question is logged so the user can settle it deliberately. Also left alone: the claim that Soul Unbound lets your body eat Explosive Cask's knockback harmlessly (whys[4], spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1]). Riot's text does not say what happens to the body when it is displaced during the spirit phase.
unverified: Whether Soul Unbound's abandoned body ignores Explosive Cask's knockback — asserted in whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1]; not derivable from Riot's text.
